# Cheese cultures

Starter cultures are bacteria added to milk to turn lactose into lactic acid, which sets the acidity and much of the flavour of the cheese. Mesophilic cultures suit cheddar and feta; thermophilic ones suit mozzarella and parmesan. Rennet follows, see [[Rennet and curds]].

Sprinkle the culture over warm milk, let it rehydrate, stir it in and hold the milk at temperature for an hour before adding rennet.

Keep freeze-dried culture sachets in the freezer, sealed against moisture.

They are close relatives of the lactic acid bacteria that sour a [[Sourdough levain]].
